title: You don’t fall in battle by accident.
paragraphs: You don’t fall in battle by accident.
You fall because you walked in weak.

Ephesians 6:10 says:
“Finally, be strong in the Lord and in His mighty power.”
Not your strength.
His.

Because let’s be honest—
your willpower fades.
Your discipline cracks.
Your secret battles? They don’t play fair.
And the enemy doesn’t fear your motivation.
He fears your connection to Christ.
But here’s what we miss…

Paul didn’t say try harder.
He didn’t say fix yourself first.
He said: be strong in the Lord.

That means your strength is borrowed.
Given.
Received.
Not earned.

You don’t win by grinding your teeth.
You win by kneeling your heart.

Because the same power that raised Jesus from the grave
is the power you’re invited to stand in.
And that changes everything.

So if you feel tired…
if temptation keeps knocking…
if your soul feels thin and worn—
Don’t pretend you’re strong.
Plug into the One who is.

Jesus is not asking you to be impressive.
He’s calling you to be dependent.

And in Him,
weak people become warriors.

From struggle to strength—
because Jesus never loses a battle.
